newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI SET TO LAUNCH INNOVATIVE CAR.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI SET TO LAUNCH INNOVATIVE CAR.

text.p: Ferrari are expected to unveil a car which irons out the reliability problems they suffered in 1996 when they launch their challenge for the 1997 Formula One world title at Maranello in Italy on Tuesday.

Double world champion Michael Schumacher of Germany, who revived Ferrari's fortunes by winning three races last year, has made it clear that he expects an improvement in reliability after a desultory run in mid-season last year.

"I expected some problems in the first year but I will not be happy if they are repeated in the second year," he said. "This time, we need to have reliability and performance so that we can win more races and mount a challenge."

It is also possible that the new Ferrari will include a radical full-width mid-wing on the car, according to some sources in Italy, as the team attempts to find a loophole in the tight, new aerodynamics section of the technical regulations.

The new Ferrari, which will run on the team's test track at Fiorano during the launch, is expected to be the last designed by British engineer John Barnard whose long spell with the team is likely to end later this year.
He is tipped to be planning to join a possible new Alain Prost-led team, if the Frenchman succeeds in purchasing the ailing Ligier outfit.

Barnard is being replaced at Ferrari by another Briton, Ross Brawn, who joined the team in December after a long and successful spell with Benetton where he worked with Schumacher and helped to guide the team to two drivers' world titles in 1994 and 1995 and one constructors' championship in 1995.
Ferrari are pursuing their first drivers' title since 1979 with Schumacher warning that it may be premature for him to be installed as favourite.
"I think Williams will still be the team to beat," he said. "But I think we will be able to challenge them more closely this time."

The early launch of the Ferrari, ahead of the new cars from Williams, McLaren and the other leading teams, may give them an advantage in the build-up to the new Formula One season which opens in Melbourne, Australia, on March 9.

Benetton have given their 1997 car an early shakedown test - - at Silverstone before Christmas -- but have not yet launched the car officially, while the new Stewart team launched theirs in mid-December but have yet to begin serious testing.
